world.title: INSPIRE Lecture Series: connecting academic education and lifelong learning in health - World Health Organization (WHO)
world.summary: The INSPIRE Lecture Series is a WHO Academy pilot initiative, developed with Université Claude Bernard Lyon 1, to connect academic education with lifelong learning for health professionals.Delivered in a blended format, the series brings together students, health professionals, academics and WHO technical experts to explore priority public health topics. It also expands access to learners and health professionals in French-speaking low- and middle-income countries.Why Attend?The INSPIRE Lecture Series offers participants the opportunity to learn from academic and WHO expertise in a shared learning environment. By linking university education with continuing professional development, the series provides evidence-based knowledge and practical perspectives on current public health priorities.For online participants, the series provides direct access to lectures delivered from the WHO Academy campus in Lyon, making high-quality learning opportunities available to the wider Francophone health workforce.Highlights Lectures co-delivered with Université Claude Bernard Lyon 1, with contributions from WHO technical experts.Priority public health topics explored through both academic expertise and WHO perspectives.A blended learning format connecting Master's students in Lyon with health professionals and learners worldwide.Live interaction and knowledge exchange among students, faculty members, WHO experts and the Francophone health workforce.Lectures delivered from the WHO Academy campus in Lyon and streamed live via Zoom.ProgrammeThe programme is being finalized.

epidemiology.title: INSPIRE Lecture Series: connecting academic education and lifelong learning in health - World Health Organization (WHO)
epidemiology.summary: The INSPIRE Lecture Series is a WHO Academy pilot initiative, developed with Université Claude Bernard Lyon 1, to connect academic education with lifelong learning for health professionals.Delivered in a blended format, the series brings together students, health professionals, academics and WHO technical experts to explore priority public health topics. It also expands access to learners and health professionals in French-speaking low- and middle-income countries.Why Attend?The INSPIRE Lecture Series offers participants the opportunity to learn from academic and WHO expertise in a shared learning environment. By linking university education with continuing professional development, the series provides evidence-based knowledge and practical perspectives on current public health priorities.For online participants, the series provides direct access to lectures delivered from the WHO Academy campus in Lyon, making high-quality learning opportunities available to the wider Francophone health workforce.Highlights Lectures co-delivered with Université Claude Bernard Lyon 1, with contributions from WHO technical experts.Priority public health topics explored through both academic expertise and WHO perspectives.A blended learning format connecting Master's students in Lyon with health professionals and learners worldwide.Live interaction and knowledge exchange among students, faculty members, WHO experts and the Francophone health workforce.Lectures delivered from the WHO Academy campus in Lyon and streamed live via Zoom.ProgrammeThe programme is being finalized.

epidemiology.title: Is artificial intelligence an aid or an adversary to the global health workforce? - World Health Organization (WHO)
epidemiology.summary: Join this FREE online webinar held by the Royal College of General Practitioners (RCGP) in collaboration with the World Health Organisation (WHO).Artificial intelligence (AI) is rapidly reshaping health systems, creating new opportunities and challenges for workforce education, management and planning. This webinar will examine how AI is influencing the skills required of health professionals, transforming workforce deployment and decision-making and shaping national and global health labour markets. Participants will explore key lessons from emerging practice, including both the benefits of AI-enabled innovation and the barriers that may limit its adoption, such as workforce readiness, regulation, ethics and equity concerns.
